Contradiction: bestPractices claims 'three corridor-mask TIFs that are pipeline INPUTS' are committed under outputs/, while frictionDiag says the waterway mask must be built by build_corridor_masks.py — are any mask TIFs tracked or on disk?

Contradiction: bestPractices/coupling say repo A (alaska-fuel-spatial-network) 'commits are authored by Diego Arias' under the jccheesman remote — who actually authored each repo, and what does that mean for the merge's ownership?
Unresolved: dataInv flags Utilities_Bulk_Fuel_Inventory.csv as DIVERGENT between repos (different md5s) and demands reconciliation — is the data actually different?
Unexamined: repo B has a second git branch feat/param-eval that no auditor mentioned — does it carry unmerged work?

Unclear: if extract_od_table.py is dead and docs are stale, how do the actual air inputs (flight_paths_combined.csv, airports_ak_dotpf.csv) reach prep_airways.py, which reads data/interim/air_flight_paths_od.csv and airports.csv?
Unexamined directory: repo A setup/ (listed in du but never described by any auditor).
Unexamined: repo A outputs/analysis/ contents and deliverable status.

Unexamined: the parent directory 02_network_analysis contains NINE sibling projects no auditor looked at (alaska_network_pipeline_mmnet, network_py, network_pipeline, network_preprocess, network_friction, network_process_workflow, network_toy_example, test_agent, test_agent_toy_example) — are any of them live consumers of the two repos or of the mmnet package, and would the merge break them?

Unresolved correctness question behind the mmnet triplication: the delivered final_network shapefiles were built with which copy, and does the newest copy's mis-snap bugfix (assemble.py roads.reset_index) mean the delivered network is potentially wrong — with what downstream consequence for the edge_id/EXPECTED-inventory contract?

Unverified auditor claims about repo A README: the phantom --skip-surfaces flag, the false 'extracts the zips' statement, the missing build_corridor_masks step, plus a possible path inconsistency for AK_Stack_150m.zip.
Missing: the identity (title/DOI/authors) of the Data-in-Brief paper the merged public repo is companion to — needed for CITATION.cff and README.
Unclear canonical home of mmnet-toolkit — does any copy declare itself canonical, and what pins the copies in place?
gap_fills:
GAP 1 — Big rasters: dataInv is right, frictionDiag wrong. Verified: /home/diegoarias/.../alaska-fuel-spatial-network has NO friction_surface/friction_inputs/, NO friction_outputs/, no AK_Stack_150m.zip, no fuel_network.duckdb, and no extracted final_network/ subdirs (only the two zips + README). A find across ~/00_academics/99_myresearch (maxdepth 4) finds AK_Stack_150m.zip and friction_inputs NOWHERE on this machine. EXTERNAL_DATA.md lines 3-13 ("ships all input datasets on disk", "Present on disk, but NOT committable") are stale for this copy — they describe Julia's machine, not this clone. Consequence for the architect: on this machine the friction half is unrunnable end-to-end; the only runnable stage from committed inputs is load_final_network.py (after manually unzipping final_network/*.zip). README.md line 104 also cites `inputs/AK_Stack_150m.zip` while .gitignore/EXTERNAL_DATA say `inputs/gee_exports/AK_Stack_150m.zip` — path drift.

GAP 2 — Corridor masks: bestPractices is wrong. `git ls-files | grep -i tif` in repo A returns ZERO files; outputs/ on disk contains no TIFs. outputs/README.md lines 18-26 still document road_mask_150m.tif, waterway_mask_150m.tif, ice_road_mask_150m.tif as written-and-consumed (stale — only the waterway mask is live in code). So outputs/waterway_mask_150m.tif is neither committed nor present, must be rebuilt via build_corridor_masks.py — whose reference grid defaults to RASTER_FILES["lulc"] (build_corridor_masks.py:74-75), i.e. the absent lulc.tif. Chain conclusion: even the mask step is unregenerable without first regenerating the 4.7GB GEE stack.

GAP 3 — Authorship: repo A's entire git history is authored by "jccheesman" and "Julia Cheesman" — NOT Diego (bestPractices' claim is wrong; the git-user-vs-remote 'mismatch' is inverted). Repo B's entire history is "Diego Arias Arana". So the merge combines two different people's repos: Julia owns the public friction repo (github.com/jccheesman), Diego owns the unpublished network repo. This explains the "the colleague's network" docstrings and "Julia's hub-facility mapping" in assemble_weighted_graph.py. The architect needs an explicit account/attribution decision (publishing org, commit authorship, CITATION.cff authors) before merging histories.

GAP 4 — Facilities CSV "divergence" is a false alarm. Parsed both with csv.reader: identical 1,901 data rows x 61 columns, identical headers, identical OBJECTID and ASTFacilityID sets, zero A-only/B-only facilities. All 656 "differing" rows differ ONLY in embedded line-ending bytes inside quoted free-text fields (Comments 499, EntityName 356, FacilityOwner 355, Recommendations_by_AEA 184, FacilityOwner_Phone 7, Tank_Operator_Info 2): the fuel-repo zip copy is UTF-8-BOM with CR terminators and \r inside fields; the mmnet copy is LF with \n inside fields. Same AEA snapshot; the merged repo just needs one normalized copy (pick LF) and a provenance note — no data reconciliation.

GAP 5 — feat/param-eval: `git log master..feat/param-eval` is EMPTY — the branch is a fully-merged ancestor of master (master is 60+ commits ahead). No unmerged work; safe to delete at merge time. Repo B is on `master`, repo A on `main` (confirmed).

GAP 6 — Air-data chain closed: scripts/normalize_raw.py SPEC entries (lines 76-82) write data/interim/airports.csv FROM data/raw/connectivity/air/airports_ak_dotpf.csv and data/interim/air_flight_paths_od.csv FROM flight_paths_combined.csv. So prep_airways.py (reads ROOT/data/interim/air_flight_paths_od.csv + airports.csv, lines 33-34) works fine with the new official data — the OLD filenames survive as interim-layer names, which is why the stale docs are confusing. extract_od_table.py confirmed dead. Note: prep_airways.py's own docstring (lines 5-6) still cites the retired raw paths data/raw/connectivity/air/air_flight_paths_od.csv + a raw airports.csv — one more stale-doc site the auditors missed.

GAP 7 — repo A setup/ (unexamined dir): two files only. setup/installations.txt — comment-only note stating root requirements.txt is the authoritative dep list, "No additional packages are required to run the three stages". setup/JETSTREAM_SETUP_GUIDE.md — optional Jetstream2 VM guide (Ubuntu, CPU-only, "no GPU or LLM backend required", venv + tmux instructions with drag-and-drop file transfer). Pure ops documentation, no pipeline logic; keep-or-drop is a taste call, but the drag-and-drop transfer instructions are pre-git-clone era and stale for a public repo.

GAP 8 — repo A outputs/analysis/: 6 tracked files — _lulc_edge_sensitivity.json, _lulc_sensitivity_buffer.json, _lulc_sensitivity_results.json, _road_grade_distribution.json, lulc_sensitivity_test.md, road_grade_distribution.md. Committed sensitivity/QA study artifacts (LULC resampling sensitivity, road grade distribution) — supplementary deliverables backing methodology choices, analogous to supplementary/cost-derivations. Keep as deliverables.

GAP 9 — hub_facility_map: grep across BOTH repos (py+md) hits only alaska-fuel-spatial-network/query_duckdb.py and assemble_weighted_graph.py (the NotImplementedError stub). No mapping file, script, or CSV exists anywhere in either repo or the sibling dirs. The routing layer's blocker is real and external — the merged-repo spec should either drop the stub+probe or document the table as future work with no in-repo source.

GAP 10 — Nine unexamined siblings in 02_network_analysis, one of which is a LIVE consumer: (a) alaska_network_pipeline_mmnet (903M, 13 commits, NO remote) — a TAPS-pipeline comparison study that builds the same Alaska network in 3 arms; its .venv editable-install finder resolves `mmnet` to the ABSOLUTE path /home/diegoarias/.../alaska_network_mmnet/mmnet-toolkit/mmnet, and scripts/run_arm.sh line 52 asserts `"mmnet-toolkit" in mmnet.__file__`; run_arm.sh line 72 also diffs against ../alaska_network_mmnet/profile.yaml. Moving/renaming alaska_network_mmnet or its mmnet-toolkit during the merge breaks this project's venv and scripts. It also confirms the same 82,300/90,921/21-component/99.7% inventory as "network of record". (b) network_py (1.1G) — "netfuel", the netweave-era Python port of the R pipeline with control plane + r_oracle; predecessor of mmnet. (c) network_preprocess (558M) + network_pipeline (355M) — the original R pipelines that netfuel/mmnet used as validation oracle. (d) network_friction (234M) — an R repo of "literature-anchored pipeline accessibility metrics", distinct from the public friction repo. (e) network_process_workflow (8.7M) — an mmnet function-walkthrough notebook project (contains yet another mmnet dir — potentially a 4th package copy). (f) network_toy_example, test_agent, test_agent_toy_example — small profile.yaml toys. None contains the missing raster data. These are archival context, but the TAPS project's hard-coded editable path and profile diff make it the one concrete external coupling the merge must not break (or must accept breaking).

GAP 11 — Which mmnet built the deliverable, and the bug question: grep confirms `roads = roads.reset_index(drop=True)` (the mis-snap fix) exists ONLY in alaska-fuel-spatial-network/mmnet-toolkit/mmnet/assemble.py:34; it is ABSENT from alaska_network_mmnet/mmnet/assemble.py (the copy pip-installed in repo B's .venv and sys.path-resolved by export_final_shapefile.py — i.e. the copy that BUILT the delivered shapefiles) and from alaska_network_mmnet/mmnet-toolkit/mmnet/assemble.py (the copy the TAPS project runs). So all shipped network data was produced by pre-fix code, and each of the three copies is 'live' for a different consumer: root mmnet = built the deliverable; B's toolkit = drives TAPS; A's toolkit = newest/fixed but drives nothing. Open architect decision the auditors never posed: either freeze the delivered network and document it was built pre-fix (keeping the EXPECTED inventory and edge_id=row-order contract valid), or rebuild with the fixed engine — which may change hub snapping, hence edge counts, hence invalidate load_final_network.py's hard-coded EXPECTED dict AND every edge_id-keyed table (edge_month_weights, edge_costs). Impact size is unquantified without a rebuild.

GAP 12 — README claims verified true: README.md line ~69 does advertise `--skip-surfaces` (flag absent from run_friction_pipeline argparse per auditors, consistent); README step 2 says load_final_network.py "Extracts final_network/network_joined_{nodes,edges}" but grep for zipfile/extract in load_final_network.py returns NOTHING — the script performs no extraction; the "Running the pipeline" section (lines 57-97) lists exactly 3 steps and never mentions build_corridor_masks.py (it appears only in the repo-layout listing, line 36).

GAP 13 — Paper identity: README.md line 3 says only "Companion code and data for the Data-in-Brief spatial-network paper" — no title, authors, DOI, or preprint link anywhere in either repo; no CITATION.cff (find confirms). The architect cannot write citation metadata from repo contents; must be supplied by the authors (Julia + Diego per gap 3).

GAP 14 — mmnet-toolkit canonical home: no copy self-declares canonical. mmnet-toolkit/README.md (identical framing in both) presents the toolkit as the shareable standalone (engine + skills/{define-network-profile, build-and-verify-network} + examples/alaska). Given gap 11's consumer map, the merge spec should promote ONE toolkit (rationally: repo A's copy, newest with 4 fixes, PLUS backports verified against a rebuild) and turn the other two locations into pointers — while handling the TAPS project's absolute-path editable install. Also confirmed: no CLAUDE.md exists in either repo (find maxdepth 2), and repo B's example_skills/ contains only copies of the friction repo's align-to-ak-stack and assign-friction-values skills plus __MACOSX junk — deletable.
